name: thin-job
about: An opening with one fact and no description: few honest angles exist.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.

output.audience: Drivers who already hold a CDL and are working or looking now, and who compare openings by what a week brings in. The sheet gives no lanes, equipment or schedule, so what stops them is the amount the opening pays per week, stated plainly.

angles.idea: Lead with what this CDL opening pays per week, stated plainly as the amount.
angles.proof: The job states what the opening pays per week.
angles.why: The amount per week is the only term the job states, so it is the strongest honest lead. Nothing has been measured yet for this carrier.

angles.idea: Lead with knowing the amount per week before you call, and what that means for planning the bills at home.
angles.proof: The job states its pay as an amount per week.
angles.why: A stated amount per week speaks to drivers who think about the household before the truck. The sheet holds no schedule, so the ad must not imply any; untested so far.

angles.idea: Lead with a parked truck that needs a licensed driver: say plainly this is a CDL driving job, then what it pays per week.
angles.proof: The job is a CDL driver opening with a stated amount per week.
angles.why: Stating the licence plainly keeps out leads who do not hold it. The sheet names no truck details, so the ad claims nothing about the equipment; untested so far.
